An integer in a Wrenfold sequence is at most 274877906943 (2^38 − 1)
The one-byte form (tag 00) encodes values 0 to 62
The two-byte form (tag 01) encodes values 0 to 16383
The three-byte form (tag 10) encodes values 0 to 4194303
The five-byte form (tag 11) encodes values 0 to 274877906943

entries.quote:
A byte 0x3F where an
integer would begin is always the end marker; inside a two-, three- or
five-byte form it is an ordinary byte of the value.
entries.statement: A byte 0x3F where an integer would begin is always the end marker; inside a two-, three- or five-byte form it is an ordinary byte of the value.

entries.quote:
the one-byte form never
holds 63, although six bits could: 63 is written in the two-byte form, as
0x40 0x3F.
entries.statement: 63 is written in the two-byte form as 0x40 0x3F, not in the one-byte form.

entries.quote: The empty sequence is the single byte 0x3F.
entries.statement: The empty sequence is the single byte 0x3F.

entries.quote: rejects exactly the inputs a decoder rejects.
entries.statement: count rejects exactly the inputs a decoder rejects.

entries.quote:
A sequence is its integers' encodings in order, followed by one end marker
byte, 0x3F.
entries.statement: encode takes a list of unsigned integers and returns their Wrenfold R3 encoded bytes.

entries.quote:
A decoder reads integers until it reaches the end marker and returns them
in order.
entries.statement: decode takes bytes and returns the list of integers encoded in them.

entries.quote:
A reader that needs only how many integers a sequence holds uses
count, which returns that number without building the list, and
rejects exactly the inputs a decoder rejects.
entries.statement: count takes bytes and returns the number of integers in the sequence without building the list.
